title: Why Pago de Arínzano tastes the way it does

lede.text: Arínzano's stony soils, low in clay, help give its wines high colour intensity and notable acidity. Mineral notes stand out in them.

chapters.title: One estate on the slopes of Montejurra
paras: Pago de Arínzano is a Vino de Pago, a protected name that belongs to one estate. The vineyard lies on the estate called Señorío de Arínzano, in the municipality of Aberin.
Aberin is in the Tierra Estella district of Navarra. The estate sits on the lower slopes of Montejurra, a mountain. The río Ega, the Ega river, runs through it.
On the south the estate ends at a small hydroelectric plant on the Ega. On the east its line follows the top of monte Santa Bárbara southward. On the west it meets the Peñazas ravine.

chapters.title: Dry, hot summers and a long season
paras: Summers here are dry and hot. At the end of summer the gap between night and day temperatures is large. The estate also has an Atlantic orientation.
Together these bring a long growing season. The grapes ripen slowly but well.
That is ideal for wines that are very aromatic, balanced and tasty, with a high content of polyphenols, the compounds behind colour and tannin.

chapters.title: The ground under the vines
paras: The soils hold a medium level of carbonates. Their texture runs from loam to sandy clay loam.
This ground also helps give the wines great quality and aromatic intensity. It gives them structure and body that last.

chapters.title: A Chardonnay white and the reds
paras: Two kinds of wine carry the name. The white is a varietal Chardonnay.
The red grapes are Tempranillo and two French varieties, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Each of the three can also make a single-variety red.
Growers tend toward planting the vines close together. The aim is to make the vines compete. That keeps the crop in check and seeks fruit with more body and extract.
Grapes are picked both by hand and by machine.
Fermentation happens in barrels and in vats of different sizes. Density and temperature are tracked throughout. Selected yeast is added.

During fermentation and the maceration after it, pump-overs (remontados) and other techniques draw out colour and aromas. Malolactic fermentation, the second fermentation, takes place in barrels and tanks.
Ageing happens in tanks and barrels of different materials and sizes, each adding its own nuance. A recent change ended the rule that ageing had to be in oak barrels only.
Every bottle shows the name Vino de Pago de Arínzano clearly on its label.
